description:
Every duplicate class counted by canon_test's ceilings (00420: 142, 00567: 15) is one closure literal whose arrow surface is read back. The views are minted (the closure's own variables), addressed (a key's positional variables, a2_p0) and instantiated (a contract's view). func_clause_empty compares literals by brand and captures, so the views are one set and separate ids.

Measured at develop c7edccd4a (full suite + 869-fixture job census):
- Intern every literal at its minted surface: 00420 duplicate classes 108 -> 5; 29 lib tests fail (callable_value_clauses and contract application read the instantiated surface).
- Literal inclusion compares surfaces: 108 -> 1; fixture 01143 and the distiller fail on all three paths (minted and addressed views of one value become different types); compile work 383,088 -> 383,429 jobs (+0.09%).
- Fold (args) -> any into fun: keys read those parameters back (axis_test pins it); type and canon tests fail.

Outcome: the ids cost identity, not work. canon_test's ceiling docs state the cause and the evidence. No pin moves. PR #594.
title: A closure type's duplicate ids are the views its readers take back out
